stack.backend: Python 3.12 / FastAPI / uv / stdlib sqlite3 (raw parameterized SQL) / pytest / ruff / mypy
stack.frontend: React 18 / TypeScript 5 / Vite / React Router / TanStack Query / CSS modules with token custom properties / Vitest / Playwright
stack.runtime: Docker Compose via init.sh, with a no-Docker uv + npm dev fallback
stack.ai: Optional backend-only Anthropic gateway, not built in M1; the domain runs fully with it off

coupling_risks: auth guard, audit writer and score function consumed across E1 to E4
money handled across DB, API and UI
policy file hash and DB row must agree

decisions.question: How does the Repository layer access SQLite?
decisions.chosen: Stdlib sqlite3 with parameterized SQL; numbered SQL migrations with SHA-256 checks; DB triggers abort UPDATE/DELETE on approved policies and schedules.
decisions.rules_out: ORMs and Alembic autogenerate or revisable migrations; any query builder that hides the SQL under the append-only triggers.
decisions.rationale: FA-F0.5 mandates checksummed SQL files; NFR-02 needs triggers; explicit SQL keeps money out of float.

decisions.question: Which frontend application stack?
options: Vite + React Router + TanStack Query + CSS modules
Vite + React Router + plain fetch hooks + CSS modules
decisions.proposed_default: Vite + React Router + TanStack Query + CSS modules
decisions.chosen: Vite SPA, React Router role-based routes, TanStack Query for server state, CSS modules over :root token custom properties, hand-built SVG charts, one component per file.
decisions.rules_out: Tailwind utility classes, Redux or global client stores for server data, and any chart library (ui_spec section 8).
decisions.rationale: Matches the UI spec token-only and own-SVG-chart rules while keeping server state cached and retried.

decisions.question: Where are the cross-epic interface contracts (auth principal, audit writer, score function) defined?
decisions.chosen: AuthPrincipal, AuditWriter and ScoreFunction are typed Protocols in the Types layer; E1 and E3 supply implementations and downstream code depends only on the Protocol.
decisions.rules_out: Services importing API-layer guards or concrete audit and score modules; adding interface stories before design.
decisions.rationale: Keeps the one-way layer rule and lets C3 and C4 start without waiting on E1 internals.

decisions.question: How is the single-command local run delivered?
decisions.chosen: init.sh builds and starts backend and frontend through Docker Compose; migrations and seeds run before the process reports ready; a no-Docker uv + npm path remains for development.
decisions.rules_out: Kubernetes, hosted deployment, and any manual multi-step bootstrap for v1.
decisions.rationale: Brief section 8.1 asks for one command; Compose is reproducible, the fallback keeps the inner loop fast.

decisions.question: How is the code organised against the layer hierarchy?
options: One package per layer on both sides
decisions.proposed_default: One package per layer on both sides
decisions.chosen: backend/src/truelend/{types,config,repository,service,api} and frontend/src/{types,config,service,api,ui}, with features as modules inside each layer; layering is enforced by an automated test (NFR-08).
decisions.rules_out: Feature-first vertical packages that blur the layer gate, and any import from a higher layer.
decisions.rationale: Architecture.md and the pre-commit layer gate assume a root/layer layout.

decisions.question: How do money values flow from database to screen?
options: Integer paise in SQLite, Decimal in code, 2-decimal strings on the wire
decisions.proposed_default: Integer paise in SQLite, Decimal in code, 2-decimal strings on the wire
decisions.chosen: Integer paise stored, Decimal in the Service layer, JSON strings with exactly 2 decimals, UI formats strings with no Number arithmetic; a static scan fails the build on float in money code.
decisions.rules_out: REAL columns, float or Number arithmetic on money anywhere, and rounding outside one shared Decimal helper.
decisions.rationale: NFR-01 and FA-F0.1; integer paise makes the append-only schedule sums exact.

decisions.question: How is authentication and authorization enforced?
options: Bearer JWT HS256 with router-level role guards
decisions.proposed_default: Bearer JWT HS256 with router-level role guards
decisions.chosen: Bearer JWT HS256, 1800 s lifetime, secret from TRUELEND_JWT_SECRET, salted password hashes, router-level dependency enforcing role at the API layer (FA-F0.2).
decisions.rules_out: Server-side session stores, an external identity provider, and role checks inside services or the UI alone.
decisions.rationale: NFR-04 requires the boundary at the controller layer; settled in the F0 feature spec.

decisions.question: How does the optional AI runtime relate to the domain?
decisions.chosen: No AI code in M1. A later gateway is backend-only behind a service interface; it proposes and the domain decides; every flow works with it disabled.
decisions.rules_out: AI calls from the UI, AI output deciding an application, and any domain import of an Anthropic SDK.
decisions.rationale: Project rule: AI proposes, the domain decides; M1 scope has no AI requirement.
